## iOS already matches — both platforms use the same visibility rules today

I checked the iOS app (`packages/ios`, pinned at `6ed85baa`, current `main`). It already implements the same queue filter as the fixed cloudlands-fe:

````swift path=packages/ios/Intent/ViewModels/ConversationViewModel.swift mode=EXCERPT
var queuedMessages: [QueuedMessage] {
    store.queuedMessages.filter {
        $0.isUserMessage
            || $0.hookWakeAttribution != nil
            || $0.prMonitorWakeAttribution != nil
            || $0.agentMessageAttribution != nil
            || $0.isEventNotificationWake
    }
}
````

`QueuedMessage.isUserMessage` in iOS uses the identical rules as the FE's `isUserQueuedMessage` (hidden iff metadata has a string `type`, non-empty `fromAgentId`, or `source == "system"`; fail-open on absent/malformed metadata), and `QueuedMessagesView` renders the four wake types as compact non-editable attribution rows explicitly marked "FE parity: QueuedMessageList". So the PR #1031 regression never affected iOS, and after FE #1120 (v2.30.1+) the two platforms are in parity.

The one open decision: both platforms currently show **user messages plus** four compact attributed rows (agent-to-agent sends, workspace-event wakes, hook wakes, PR-monitor wakes) — a deliberate design from FE #1120 and mirrored on iOS. If you literally want **only user messages** on both, that's a behavior change to both repos, not a parity fix. Let me confirm which you want before speccing any work.
